In this book we describe a particular approach to interaction design that we call the Goal-Directed Design method. We’ve found that when designers focus on people’s goals—the reasons why they use a product in the first place—as well as their expecta - tions, attitudes, and aptitudes, they can devise solutions that people find both powerful and pleasurable to use.
